newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB rallies on digital news.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB rallies on digital news.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc rose by more than three percent on Wednesday, bolstered by news that it is moving ahead on its digital television venture, dealers and analysts said.
The stock, up for a third consecutive session, was up 20p to 615-1/2 at 0849 GMT. The stock has risen 38-1/2p, or 6.7 percent, during the last three sessions.

BSkyB said it placed orders for one million set top boxes, and that it would join forces with British Telecommunications Plc, Midland Bank and Matsushita Electric forming a new company to deliver digital interactive services to television viewers in the UK. It projected profitability for the venture after five years. nFLLU5702F.
BSkyB also posted third quarter pre-tax profits of 81.6 million stg, a bit weaker than some analysts had forecast.
"The figures and subscriber numbers were a bit disappointing, but I think the stock is moving on this digital news," said one market maker.

"The deal finally has been clarified," an analyst said. "They've ordered the set-top boxes and we have some figures to use. That they're in with BT means they'll get interactive services off the ground."
Analysts said the market also was relieved by the pro-rata investment of 265 million pounds to establish the infrastructure for the new services and subsidise the digital satellite boxes.
"There were some huge numbers being thrown around that were frightening people. This is a sensible number," the analyst added.
Elsewhere, shares the UK companies that will provide the set-top boxes also rose. Shares in Amstrad advanced 10p to 228-1/2, while shares in Pace Micro Technology Plc firmed 1/2p to 88.
The other two non-UK companies contracted to provide the boxes are Matsushita and Grundig/Hyundai. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
